Long Storyboard: This is the first crack in the official story. The route promised safety, but the cart is ruined, the driver is dead, and the system’s response is decorative. Run this scene as threshold into branded wilderness and first moral test: The overturned cart gives the party a mystery before it gives them a fight. Keep the camera close to practical choices, visible consequences, and the difference between ordinary people and the infrastructure pressing on them.
Read Aloud: A vendor cart lies sideways across the road. Produce and invoices spill into the mud. A polished placard blinks: INCIDENT RESPONSE EXPECTED WITHIN 3–5 BUSINESS DAYS.

Gm Notes: The placard can be a standard route-monitoring glyph, not proof that anyone meaningfully knows what happened. Keep player-facing information actionable. Reveal systemic truth through objects, reactions, and consequences before naming it. Sablewood route lore: this is an approved path, and the body/cart disruption should feel like a coverage failure as much as a wilderness event. Manufactured-threat lens: seed the contradiction, do not explain it. The surface goal stays simple and heroic. [KEEP/EARNED] The driver died from a cut throat; the strixwolf did not kill him. (Instinct or Knowledge Medium 15) [ADD/EARNED] Near the cart is a pre-written Grail "Hazard Confirmed: Strixwolf Attack" tag. (Finesse or Instinct Medium 15)
Sensory Details: split apple skins wet rope blood under wheel-ruts instead of claw marks Sunken road walls press close enough to feel like a product corridor carved through something ancient.
Body Language: Marlowe steps between the crate and the wreck Garrick kneels before touching anything Barnacle scans for whoever benefits
Sample Dialogue: Garrick Reed Animals scatter. People arrange a scene.

Checks: Instinct or Knowledge Separate animal scavenging from staged violence. Standard The PCs learn Tamsin was likely killed by humanoids. 15 Cleanly resolve: Separate animal scavenging from staged violence. Add a concrete boon, extra clue, or improved position. Success, plus the player names one helpful detail or asks one follow-up question. Success, but the GM exposes a cost, ticks a countdown, or reveals a new pressure tied to The Overturned Vendor Cart. The full goal slips, but the party still learns a useful truth or avoids the worst consequence. The GM makes a hard move that follows from the fiction and leaves the next choice visible. Spend Fear to separate true evidence from a tempting false read, or put the carriage/cargo under time pressure. On mixed or sliding results, reveal information in layers: visible fact, actionable clue, then systemic truth.

Choices Consequences: Investigate carefully More clues, less surprise pressure. Bramble Union feels discoverable. Rush to blame the creature The moral test tightens. Strixwolf Blood Debt becomes possible.

Clues: Route Ledger The delivery was delayed. Someone manipulated the logistics trail. The ledger's time marks do not match the official route. Bramble Strand Someone else was here. Bramble Union scouts marked the site. A tied plant-fiber marker under the cart. Earned seed Available if players investigate, show mercy, or ask the right question. The driver died from a cut throat; the strixwolf did not kill him. Instinct or Knowledge Medium 15 Earned seed Available if players investigate, show mercy, or ask the right question. Near the cart is a pre-written Grail "Hazard Confirmed: Strixwolf Attack" tag. Finesse or Instinct Medium 15

Loot: Use Vendor Cart and Tamsin Vell search tables Keystone Asset™: Inside the sealed crate, packed in wax-paper and reassurance, sits a heavy grey stone the size of a loaf, warm to the touch, faintly humming, with a light deep inside it that is slowly going out. Incident Response Placard™: A flat brass disc on a post holds a watchful glyph and a single cheerful bell. When trouble happens nearby, the glyph lights, the bell rings once, brightly, and then nothing else happens at all. Sableblade: Growing straight up out of dark forest soil, like a sapling that decided to be a sword, is a blade of living dark wood and pale metal. It has no maker's mark and hums when your hand nears the hilt. Recall Stone: A smooth grey pebble feels warm and ordinary until it refuses to stay where you put it. Set it down, look away, and it waits back in your palm. Goldwater Liability Token™: A heavy brass chit with a smiling coin-face drops into your palm like a tiny verdict. The fine print is too small to read without feeling blamed. Tamsin's Home-Token: A small thumb-polished token on a cord hangs beside the torn blue scarf, warm from wear and etched with a tiny house mark instead of a company seal...

Reveal Hooks: Loreborne or Knowledge-focused PCs can read the institutional layer. Wildborne/community-focused PCs can read local custom and ecological stress. Martial/security-focused PCs can read threat posture and custody logic. Magic-focused PCs can feel ward tone, soul-signal, or spell instability. Loreborne: spots older legal, heraldic, or ward-craft language under the branding. Underborne: notices service doors, hidden routes, and who built the thing nobody credits. Highborne: reads etiquette, class panic, and reputational risk. Ridgeborne: notices stonework, weight, pressure, and structural weakness. Wildborne: reads the land, animals, and local ecological stress. Elf/Ribbet/Human/Giant/Katari: invite one sensory or social detail from the player's heritage. Sorcerer/Rogue/Warrior/Guardian/Ranger: give each class one table-facing way to shine without changing the plot.

Fear Spends: Spend Fear to separate true evidence from a tempting false read, or put the carriage/cargo under time pressure. Make the safe road feel less safe: noise, scent, cracked wheel, or cargo hum. Separate evidence from assumption so a monster read is tempting but incomplete.

Story Scope: Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end. Every act offers at least one guaranteed and one earned hint that the danger is manufactured and the forest is not the enemy. The Strixwolf Mother is feeding pups and guarding them; she reacts to tone, not bloodlust.
